datasets_evaluated.evidence: In this work, we evaluate FreAD’s performance using three datasets for encrypted traffic anomaly detection in ICS: CTU13 [28], IDS2018 [25], and DoHBrw-2020 (DoH2020) [29].

feature_groups.evidence: F3EM to extract features from encrypted data flows, effectively alleviating the representation information bottleneck associated with traditional DL-based point-by-point mapping anomaly detection methods.

tls_versions_stated.evidence: This dataset captures various botnet attacks in a university network, utilizing hypertext transfer protocol secure (HTTPS) and transport layer security (TLS) 1.3 protocols.

model_family.value: Deep learning (Frequency-domain feature fusion encoding, anomaly scoring network)
model_family.evidence: FreAD utilizes a frequency-domain feature fusion encoding module to capture global temporal dependencies. An anomaly scoring network integrates a small amount of labeled data along with pseudolabeled data generated from the modified Z-score algorithm.

shortcut_check.evidence: In this comprehensive evaluation, we investigate the critical contributions of each component within the F3EM in the FreAD framework. By systematically removing key component: FDTL, TDCL, reconstruction (Rec), prediction (Pre), and FDPM.

metrics.evidence: We employed three widely recognized evaluation metrics to assess the performance of FreAD: AUC-ROC, AUC-PR, and F1-score.

granularity.evidence: Specifically, FreAD leverages a frequency-domain feature fusion encoding module (F3EM) to extract features from encrypted data flows, overcoming the limitations of traditional DL-based methods that rely on point-by-point mapping for anomaly detection.

cost_reported.evidence: We analyzed six key metrics: memory usage (MB), max memory usage (MB), running time (ms), inference speed (FPS), floating point operations per second (FLOPs), and parameters.
